newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Walsh bewails illegal liquor sales in Tallaght.
newsitem.headline: Walsh bewails illegal liquor sales in Tallaght.

text.p: Illegal off-licences in Tallaght are blackmailing young people into buying alcohol from them, a parliamentary committee was told Wednesday.
"Blackmail is operating in west Tallaght", Deputy Eamon Walsh told the Legislation and Security committee.
A network of these outlets had been set up in housing estates in west Tallaght and were selling alcohol worth about 20,000 punts a week, he said.

Unmarried mothers were being threatened that if they did not buy a certain amount of drink every week from these outlets, that they would be reported to the Department of Social Welfare for having what he termed "an unannounced lodger".
Some mothers had been forced to hand over their Social Welfare children's allowance books, as security for the alcohol.
They were also encouraging under-age drinking by offering alcohol on credit and then threatening violence, if the drink was not paid for.
The Deputy said a criminal element was behind this network which operated along the same lines as drug pushers.
He believed they would continue to develop until reasonable laws for the legitimate off-licences were introduced.

The Deputy was speaking after the Licensed Vintners Association, (LVA) which represents about 600 pubs in the greater Dublin area, had called for pub closing time to be extended to 12.30 a.m., every day, with "drinking-up" time of another 30 minutes.
They were criticised by the government backbencher, Deputy Alan Shatter, who said there was no logical reason to name any hour as closing time.
The law was largely ignored at present as those who want late-night drinking can go to a nightclub, where alcohol is served "until all hours", he said.
"Then two or three times a year the police raid these clubs and people are very slow at opening the doors to the police, while all the bottles are put away", he said.
Frank Fell, chief executive of the LVA, admitted that a significant number of his members would support the view that they should be free to close their pubs when they want to.
But as they did not believe they would get that, they wanted closing time extended to 12.30 a.m. every night of the week, he said.
